title: ASIC's powers to suspend, cancel and vary AFS licences and make banning orders
subject: This guide describes the administrative powers available to ASIC to enforce compliance with the financial services licensing provisions under the Corporations Act, including the suspension, cancellation, and variation of Australian Financial Services (AFS) licences and the making of banning orders. It sets out the matters ASIC generally takes into account when exercising these powers.
background: The guide is issued under the ASIC Act and the Corporations Act to explain ASIC's enforcement approach regarding AFS licensees and their representatives. It is intended for AFS licensees, their representatives, and advisers who need to understand ASIC's administrative enforcement powers and the circumstances in which those powers may be exercised.
ruling: ASIC will take administrative action—such as suspending, cancelling, or varying an AFS licence or making a banning order—when it appears that a licensee or person has contravened the Corporations Act, provided false or misleading information, or is no longer fit and proper. ASIC indicates that it will consider the nature, seriousness, and impact of the contravention, any prior history of compliance, and the likelihood of future compliance when deciding whether to act. The guide emphasises that ASIC's powers are discretionary and that ASIC may issue a banning order at the same time or following suspension or cancellation. ASIC also states that it will afford procedural fairness to affected persons, such as through a hearing process before making a final decision.
